lesson.title: Practice: G <-> C — 1-minute changes
lesson.one_line_promise: Build fluency on G <-> C until 30+ clean changes/min.
objectives: Run a 1-minute G <-> C change count
Hit 30 clean changes/min (advance) and aim for 60 (goal)
Let the app remember your weak pairs for spaced review

C.name: C major (Lauren's 'easy C' — 2-finger reduction)
C.note: Reduced 2-finger C voicing for confidence-building. Spelling verified deterministically by chord-theory-check.js (2026-08-08) as C E G. 'Lauren's easy C' is a teaching label; arithmetic proves the fingering spells C major and is playable.

exercises.name: The four-bar loop — G <-> C
exercises.purpose: Drill G <-> C as taught in the lesson.
exercises.coaching: Metronome on. G to C, back and forth, as many clean changes as you can in one minute.

exercises.name: 1-minute change drill — G <-> C
exercises.purpose: Count completed G <-> C changes in 60s; the 30/60 engine records your rate into the fluency memory.
exercises.coaching: Metronome on. G to C, back and forth, as many clean changes as you can in one minute. The app remembers this pair — your weakest pairs come back for spaced review automatically.

avatar_coaching_copy.intro: Today we drill G <-> C. Clean, even changes — not fast messy ones.
avatar_coaching_copy.results: A higher count than last time means your hands are learning. That is the only metric that matters here.
avatar_coaching_copy.wrap: Logged to your fluency memory. If this pair is weak, it will resurface in review.
